intent.purpose: Track all known deviations from spec and unresolved ambiguities in the harness
intent.scope: Gap and ambiguity entries only. NOT the filing process (gap-governance.md rule). NOT the framework documentation (framework-gap-governance.md). NOT gap reference files (reference/gap-*.md)
intent.audience: /gap skill, /gaps skill, /audit skill, agents checking whether a deficiency has already been filed

gaps.title: Hook scripts deployed without backup or interactive review
gaps.observation: setup-user-hooks.sh/.ps1 use direct cp/Copy-Item for hook scripts. No backup_file call before overwrite, no deploy_managed_file interactive review, no adopt/skip/merge options.
gaps.expected: .claude/rules/managed-file-deployment.md requires backup before write and interactive diff review for shell script deployment type. .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md requires backup before overwrite.
gaps.impact: User customizations to hook scripts in ~/.claude/hooks/ are silently overwritten on every aitools install. No way to review changes or adopt local modifications back to source.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: managed-file-deployment.md, config-file-safety.md, setup-user-hooks.sh. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Upgrade to deploy_managed_file (same as markdown type). Adopt target: shared/hooks/<filename> in aitools repo.

gaps.title: Bash scripts missing backup_file before JSON config merge
gaps.observation: setup-user-hooks.sh and setup-user-mcp.sh do NOT call backup_file before settings.json merge. Their PowerShell counterparts DO call Backup-File.
gaps.expected: .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md 'Backup before overwrite': caller MUST call backup_file / Backup-File before the merge write for JSON config type.
gaps.impact: If a bash merge corrupts settings.json, there is no backup to restore from. PowerShell has the backup. Platform parity violation — same operation has different safety guarantees per platform.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: config-file-safety.md, setup-user-hooks.sh, setup-user-mcp.sh, their .ps1 counterparts. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Add backup_file call in bash scripts before Node.js merge, matching the PowerShell pattern.

gaps.title: JSON config merges have no interactive review
gaps.observation: All JSON config merges proceed silently. Clobber detection blocks on field loss, but there is no 'here is what will change, proceed?' prompt showing managed field diffs.
gaps.expected: .claude/rules/interactive-menus.md defines JSON field-level review with current → proposed display. No setup script implements this pattern for JSON configs.
gaps.impact: Users cannot review what changed in settings.json, cli-config.json, or mcp.json before the write. Silent merges erode trust — users don't know what aitools changed on their machine.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: interactive-menus.md, setup-user-hooks.sh, setup-user-mcp.sh, setup-user-cursor.sh. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Add field-level review menu showing changed managed fields with old → new values. Pattern defined in interactive-menus.md 'JSON field-level review'.

gaps.title: Cursor MCP disable is project-scoped, not user-scoped
gaps.observation: agent mcp disable stores disable state per-project, not per-user. Setup script runs from the aitools repo directory only. Other projects see vercel/webflow as enabled.
gaps.expected: .claude/rules/tool-lifecycle.md 'MCP server disable scope' documents this asymmetry. No setup script accounts for it.
gaps.impact: Projects other than aitools see vercel/webflow MCP servers as enabled, causing authentication errors on Cursor Agent CLI launch. Users must manually disable in each project.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: tool-lifecycle.md MCP sections, setup-cursor-ide-mcp.sh. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Stop deploying vercel/webflow to user-level mcp.json. Add per-project only via aitools --addmcp.

gaps.title: Directory backups cascade — each backup contains older backups
gaps.observation: backup_dir copies the entire directory including individual .bak.* files from previous backups. Each new backup contains all older backups.
gaps.expected: .claude/rules/config-file-safety.md defines retention limits (5 directory backups) but backup_dir does not exclude .bak.* patterns from the copy.
gaps.impact: Backup directories grow geometrically. A directory with 5 backups where each contains the previous creates cascading storage growth.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: aitools-lib.sh backup_dir function, config-file-safety.md. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Exclude *.bak.* patterns from directory backup copies in both bash and PS1 implementations.

gaps.title: README 22 versions behind — missing major features
gaps.observation: README.md last updated at v0.33. Current version is v0.54.1. Missing: logging locations, sessions feature, troubleshooting, env vars (AITOOLS_FORCE/DRY_RUN/RUN_ID), MCP status, config.json format, check scripts, governance framework.
gaps.expected: Document intent design principle: every markdown file must state its purpose and be current. README is the first file new users see.
gaps.impact: New users or contributors cannot understand what aitools does or how to use it without reading source code. The README describes a project 22 versions ago.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: README.md, RELEASE_NOTES.md version history. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Full README rewrite covering current CLI, features, governance framework, and troubleshooting.

gaps.title: AITOOLS_FORCE/DRY_RUN/RUN_ID env vars undocumented
gaps.observation: Entry points set AITOOLS_FORCE, AITOOLS_DRY_RUN, AITOOLS_RUN_ID, AITOOLS_SUPPRESS_SUMMARY_DISPLAY env vars used by child scripts. Not documented in README, CLAUDE.md, or any reference file.
gaps.expected: No spec exists for: env var documentation convention. Only discoverable by reading source code.
gaps.impact: Users cannot script around aitools or understand its behavior in CI without reading the entry point source. Env vars are a public interface without documentation.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools, scripts/aitools.ps1. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Document in /aitools skill and README. Add to CLAUDE.md Build & Run section.

gaps.title: Sessions feature silently fails without userRepoPath
gaps.observation: aitools sessions subcommands produce confusing output or silently fail if userRepoPath is not configured in ~/.aitools/config.json.
gaps.expected: PSO: Fail, don't mask. Missing configuration should surface via log_error with remediation instructions.
gaps.impact: Users who haven't run 'aitools user init' get confusing behavior instead of a clear error telling them what to do.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools sessions subcommand handlers. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Add explicit check for userRepoPath at the start of sessions subcommands. log_error with 'Run aitools user init to configure session archiving'.

gaps.title: Entry point logging override pattern has unclear design intent
gaps.observation: Entry points redefine log/log_ok/log_error/log_warn after sourcing aitools-lib. If lib adds a new logging function, overrides miss it. No validation that overrides cover all levels.
gaps.expected: No spec exists for: when and how entry points may override library functions. script-standards.md documents the logging helpers but not the override pattern.
gaps.impact: If aitools-lib adds a new log level (e.g., log_detail), entry point overrides silently miss it. Log output from the new level would use the lib default format instead of the entry point's custom format. Inconsistent log output.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools, aitools-lib.sh logging functions. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Clarify in /logging skill and script-standards whether this is intentional specialization or tech debt. If intentional, document the contract (which functions entry points must override). If tech debt, consider an explicit delegation pattern.

gaps.title: No CI pipeline — all verification is manual check scripts
gaps.observation: No GitHub Actions workflow exists. All verification relies on manual check script invocation. PSO says 'checklist scripts, not ad-hoc' but nothing enforces running them before commit/push.
gaps.expected: No spec exists for: whether CI is required for this project, or whether hooks + skills are the intended replacement for CI in AI-assisted workflows.
gaps.impact: Human commits (outside AI sessions) have no automated guardrails. AI sessions have the PreToolUse git checklist hook (planned, governance plan step 8) but it's not built yet. Check scripts exist but are voluntary.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: .github/ (empty), check scripts, PSOs. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Decide: is CI needed for a single-developer project with AI-assisted sessions? Options: 1) GitHub Actions running check scripts on push, 2) git pre-commit/pre-push hooks (local enforcement), 3) accept current state (hooks + skills replace CI for AI sessions, human commits are rare). Document the decision.

gaps.title: CLI entry point behavior only discoverable by reading source
gaps.observation: Entry point dispatch (noargs vs install vs gitpull vs user init), quiet pull retry logic, network detection, flag passthrough to install scripts — not documented in any reference file or skill.
gaps.expected: Document intent design principle: every file must state its purpose. Entry points are consumed by users but have no user-facing documentation.
gaps.impact: Users cannot understand aitools CLI behavior without reading the bash/PS1 source. Debugging failed runs requires source-level knowledge.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: scripts/aitools, README.md. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Create /aitools skill (user-level) documenting CLI modes, flags, env vars, and dispatch logic. Create /aitools-dev skill (project-level) documenting how to add new subcommands.

gaps.title: Cursor skill deployment mechanism unverified
gaps.observation: setup-user-mcp deploys skills to ~/.cursor/skills/. Whether Cursor Agent CLI discovers and loads SKILL.md files from that path has never been tested.
gaps.expected: No spec exists for: Cursor skill discovery mechanism. Cursor docs do not confirm ~/.cursor/skills/ as a discovery path.
gaps.impact: Deploying to ~/.cursor/skills/ may be wasted work (files ignored) or may cause unexpected behavior. Decision made 2026-03-14: deploy to Claude Code only via setup-user-skills.sh/.ps1. Cursor deployment deferred until this ambiguity is resolved.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Confirmed during step 4 prerequisite work. Audited: Cursor docs, agent CLI behavior. Session: 2026-03-13, revisited 2026-03-14.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Test Cursor skill discovery: create a skill in ~/.cursor/skills/, launch agent CLI, check if it's loaded. If yes, add Cursor deployment back to setup-user-skills. If no, close this gap and remove Cursor skill code from setup-user-mcp.

gaps.title: Skill deployment hardcoded for 2 skills, needs dynamic discovery
gaps.observation: setup-user-mcp.sh:L378-379 and setup-user-mcp.ps1:L370-371 hardcode two deploy_skill calls (chrome-devtools, a11y-debugging). Five skills exist in shared/skills/ but only two are deployed. Skill deployment is bundled into setup-user-mcp despite being a separate concern.
gaps.expected: CLAUDE.md 'Skills as enablement' design principle: every managed tool gets a skill. .claude/rules/gap-governance.md surfacing duty and governance plan decision #20 require skill deployment infrastructure before building more skills.
gaps.impact: New skills created in shared/skills/ are invisible to Claude Code until manually hardcoded into setup-user-mcp. 3+ skills (planning, optimize-plan, investigate, intent-writing, intent-audit) exist in source but are not deployed. Blocks the entire skill-based governance architecture.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design. Confirmed during step 4 prerequisite work (2026-03-14). Audited: setup-user-mcp.sh, shared/skills/, ~/.claude/skills/. Session: 2026-03-13, revisited 2026-03-14.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Create new setup-user-skills.sh/.ps1 script pair. Dynamic iteration over shared/skills/*/ directories. Deploy to ~/.claude/skills/ only (Cursor deferred per gap #12). Remove skill deployment code from setup-user-mcp. Wire into entry points (scripts/aitools, scripts/aitools.ps1, scripts/aitools-install.sh/.ps1) and build-deploy.sh.

gaps.title: No meta-skill for teaching ambiguity detection
gaps.observation: Surfacing duty is defined in gap-governance rule (always loaded). /audit provides deep review. No skill teaches agents HOW to identify ambiguities in documentation — the pattern recognition itself.
gaps.expected: No spec exists for: ambiguity detection methodology as a teachable skill. Surfacing duty says 'look for ambiguities' but doesn't teach how.
gaps.impact: Agents follow the surfacing duty mechanically (check cross-references, check for contradictions) but may miss subtle ambiguities that require reading comprehension and domain knowledge.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Consider whether /intent-audit partially addresses this (it checks content against stated intent, which catches many ambiguities). If a separate meta-skill is still needed, build as user-level skill teaching documentation analysis patterns.

gaps.title: Bridge pattern cross-reference points to missing section
gaps.observation: script-standards.md references 'See script-standards-detail.md Bridge pattern' but that section heading does not exist in reference/script-standards-detail.md.
gaps.expected: Cross-reference convention: every @reference must point to existing content. /audit skill scope includes cross-reference validation.
gaps.impact: Agent following the reference finds no content. The bridge pattern (check-lib double-init) is documented elsewhere in the file but not under the expected heading.
gaps.discoveryContext: Filed during governance plan design session. Audited: script-standards.md, script-standards-detail.md headings. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Add 'Bridge pattern' section heading to script-standards-detail.md above the existing double-init documentation. Or fix the reference in script-standards.md to point to the correct heading.

gaps.title: Skills claimed discoverable but deployment infrastructure missing
gaps.observation: Session created 4 user-level skills in shared/skills/ (planning, optimize-plan, investigate, rca) and stated they would be available after restart. shared/skills/ is the source directory, not the deployment target.
gaps.expected: Governance plan decision #20: 'shared/skills/ is source, not deployment. Skills are invisible to Claude Code until deployed to ~/.claude/skills/.' CLAUDE.md 'Specs vs state': never describe a feature as working if it hasn't fired in production.
gaps.impact: User told skills would be available after restart. They are not. Trust erosion — agent described a feature as working that has never been deployed.
gaps.discoveryContext: Found during governance plan step 3 wrap-up. The agent knew about gap #15 but didn't connect it to the suggestion being made. Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Resolves when gap #15 is fixed (setup-user-skills with dynamic discovery). No separate action needed.

gaps.title: Reference file placed without evaluating alternatives
gaps.observation: path-targeted-hooks-analysis.md was created in reference/ without evaluating alternative locations or consulting the user. Decision criteria from foundational decision #16 were not applied.
gaps.expected: Governance plan decision #16: apply 6-point evaluation criteria (state, context, leverage, risk, precedent, ambiguity) when suggesting. Source-of-truth protection framework: placement decisions for reference files affect downstream consumers.
gaps.impact: Work product placed without deliberation. Precedent set for skipping placement evaluation. The assumption was treated as obvious when it wasn't — alternatives included section in governance plan, plans/ file, or .scratch/ until hooks are built.
gaps.discoveryContext: Found during governance plan step 3 wrap-up. Initially filed as 'reference file created without review gate' — corrected to 'unexamined assumption about placement.' Session: 2026-03-13.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Evaluate placement with user applying decision criteria. Options: 1) reference/ standalone (current), 2) section in governance plan, 3) plans/ as hook implementation plan, 4) defer until hooks are built.

gaps.title: No process discipline rule governs plan adherence or deviations
gaps.observation: During governance plan step 4 prerequisite work, agent proposed pulling step 7 (/aitools-dev skill) forward to before step 4, framing it as 'the skill is small.' No rule, reference, or principle defines what constitutes a process deviation, when resequencing is acceptable, or how to formally amend a plan before executing out of order.
gaps.expected: No spec exists for: plan adherence, process deviations, plan amendment protocols. Audited: CLAUDE.md design principles (governance, ambiguity, specs-vs-state — none address process), .claude/rules/gap-governance.md (tracks defects, not process), .claude/rules/plan-execution.md (code batch mechanics, not sequencing discipline), /planning skill (plan creation strategy), /optimize-plan skill (plan review, not adherence).
gaps.impact: Plan steps can be resequenced ad-hoc without formal amendment. Deviations are invisible — no record of what was skipped or pulled forward, or why. The governance plan's sequential dependencies exist to prevent prerequisites from being bypassed.
gaps.discoveryContext: Executing governance plan step 4 prerequisites (SubagentStart hook). Agent needed /aitools-dev skill (step 7) for wiring guidance. User identified the pull-forward proposal as a process deviation lacking formal justification. Audited: CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/gap-governance.md, .claude/rules/plan-execution.md, /planning skill, /optimize-plan skill. Session: 2026-03-14.
gaps.frameworks: Process deviation (ISO/quality management — doing something outside established procedure requires documentation and justification), double-loop learning (Argyris — the framework itself needed to grow, not just the plan), change management protocols (amend first, execute second).
gaps.suggestedResolution: Create user-level rule ~/.claude/rules/process-discipline.md covering: plan adherence (steps are sequential contracts), process deviation (definition, documentation, approval), plan amendment protocol (amend first, execute second), prerequisite pull-forward (when a later step is genuinely needed earlier, amend with rationale). Add design principle to CLAUDE.md. Alternative: extend .claude/rules/gap-governance.md with a process section — but process discipline is broader than gap governance and applies across all projects, so a separate user-level rule is preferred.

gaps.title: Tool registry is markdown — needs migration to three-layer pattern
gaps.observation: reference/tool-registry.md is a large markdown file serving as both structured data and prose documentation. reference/tool-versions.json tracks versions separately. Two sources that can drift.
gaps.expected: CLAUDE.md 'Three-layer registries' design principle: every registry follows rule + JSON + skill pattern. Markdown registry files are not sources of truth — they drift from structured data.
gaps.impact: Tool data is not machine-readable for /audit validation. Version data drifts between tool-registry.md and tool-versions.json. No /tools read skill for agents to access tool data in context. No per-tool reference files for detailed tool documentation.
gaps.discoveryContext: Identified while establishing the three-layer registry convention during framework adoption work. Audited: tool-registry.md, tool-versions.json, framework-adoption.md registry convention. Session: 2026-03-14.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Migrate to: tool-registry.json (structured data, single source of truth), per-tool reference files (reference/tool-*.md), /tools read skill, /tool-eval write skill. Existing tool-lifecycle.md rule stays. Large effort — plan as a roadmap item.

gaps.title: Gap registry has no read/context skill
gaps.observation: /gap skill files entries (write). /audit skill checks health. No skill presents the gap registry with context for agents working with gaps (read).
gaps.expected: CLAUDE.md 'Three-layer registries' design principle: every registry has a read skill that presents the data with context.
gaps.impact: Agents must read known-gaps.json directly and interpret the schema themselves. No skill provides context (related gaps, framework references, discovery cycle guidance) when reviewing existing gaps.
gaps.discoveryContext: Identified while establishing the three-layer registry convention. Audited: gap skill (write-only), audit skill (health-only), framework-adoption.md registry convention. Session: 2026-03-14.
gaps.suggestedResolution: Create /gaps read skill (project-level). Reads known-gaps.json, presents gaps with context (severity distribution, stale items, linked plans, framework references). Distinct from /gap (filing) and /audit (health checking).

closed.title: Skill priority was wrong in plan v0.54
Subagent skill preloading — additionalContext verified via docs
